reconcile.connective: Defenders read "righteous" as God's verdict on Lot's general course of life, not an endorsement of the daughter-offering or the incest.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, the upstream source of this entry, who holds that 2 Peter's calling Lot "just" and "righteous" cannot be squared with the same man offering his virgin daughters to a rape mob and fathering children by both of them while drunk.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Lot righteous?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/lot_righteous.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; print ed. 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: God does not account men just or unjust from one single act, but from their general course of life.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the contradiction: the 'righteous' label of 2 Pet 2:7 is a verdict on Lot's general life, so the single bad acts of Gen 19:8/19:30-36 do not negate it. Strongest single harmonization; parity-capped to one to match the named-skeptic discrepancy pole on this discrepancy_first row.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14), on 2 Peter 2:7
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this exact tension at 2 Peter 2:7, arguing God reckons a man just or unjust by his general course of life rather than a single act, while frankly conceding Lot's sins in Genesis 19. Used in place of Haley, whose specific coverage of this moral-character discrepancy could not be confirmed.
